title: Countable & Uncountable
description: Distinguish items that can be counted from food substances and liquids.
objectives: Distinguish items that can be counted from food substances and liquids.

stages.title: Understand the language
stages.instructions: Read the explanation, examples, common error, and recap.

blocks.text: This lesson prepares you to distinguish items that can be counted from food substances and liquids. The central language is a/an, plural nouns, and uncountable nouns. It belongs to the practical context of food & café english. Focus first on meaning: decide what information the listener needs. Then choose the subject, verb form, and useful detail. At A1, keep the message short and concrete. One clear sentence is enough before the other person responds. The same language returns in the listening, repeat, speaking, exercises, and guided conversation stages.

blocks.title: Pattern
blocks.text: a/an, plural nouns, and uncountable nouns

blocks.english: I have an apple and two sandwiches.
blocks.explanation: Use this model to begin the countable & uncountable exchange.

blocks.english: We need some rice and water.
blocks.explanation: This countable & uncountable model adds a different detail or response.
Use this question or response to keep the countable & uncountable exchange moving.

blocks.text: Notice the two models: “I have an apple and two sandwiches.” and “We need some rice and water.” They show the pattern in complete communication, not as isolated grammar. Say the model aloud, replace one detail, and check that the new sentence keeps the intended meaning. When the other person asks a follow-up question, answer directly and add a relevant detail. This makes the exchange natural while keeping the language controlled.

blocks.title: Common error
blocks.text: Do not mix the word order or verb form with another pattern. Keep the controlled form for this lesson: a/an, plural nouns, and uncountable nouns.
